Please send me the text of the new law.

I run finance for the European entities, and every quarter somebody from Brazil explains the tax system to me. Every quarter I get lost after the first minute. It is not their English. It is the order. They start with the history, then the five taxes, then the exceptions, and the number I need arrives at the very end, when I have stopped listening. So here is what I ask now. Tell me what changes, in one sentence. Tell me what it costs us, or what it saves us. Tell me what you need from me. If I want the mechanism, I will ask for it. I trust my people in Brazil. I do not need to understand the whole system to make a decision. I need to understand the impact.

I have worked on tax projects in India for twelve years, and we went through our own reform in 2017, when the country moved to a single goods and services tax. I learned one thing the hard way. If you give the global team only the number, they do not trust it. They see a big change, they do not understand where it comes from, and they ask for a second opinion. That costs you weeks. So I always give them the mechanism first, in a very simple way. One comparison with something they already know. In Europe they have a VAT, so I say: it works like your VAT, and here is the one difference. Then the number. When they understand the logic, the number stops being scary.
